judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Arvind Dharmadhikari, C.J.:— Heard on admission.

2. The present writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following relief:

“For the reasons stated in the accompanying affidavit, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue a Writ of Mandamus, or any other Writ, order or direction in the nature of Writ, forbearing the respondents herein from interfering with the petitioner's peaceful possession of their property measuring 27.59 acres comprised in Survey Numbers 389/2A1A1, 384, 398/2, 397/2, 390/1C1, 391/1A, 380/1, 379/1A and 392 and also 765/29B2C and 765/29B1 in Mangadu Village, Sriperumbudur Taluk, Kancheepuram District except under due process of law and pass such further or other orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper and thus render justice.”

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, after obtaining necessary approval from CMDA, the petitioner has developed a large residential project comprising villas and apartments at Mangadu Village. The petitioner is in lawful possession of the lands measuring 27.59 acres comprised in various survey numbers stated in the writ petition and out of 27.59 acres, the petitioner had gifted 3.91 acres in favour of the first respondent Municipality for the purposes of laying load and Open Space Reservation and that the layout and building plans have also been duly approved by the CMDA.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that for the purpose of advertisement of its project, the petitioner erected advertisement boards/unipoles in the year 2016 on its own lands and since then no untoward incident took place. The petitioner had also submitted application seeking approval/licence under the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Act, 1998. While the petitioner's application was pending consideration, the first respondent issued notices directing removal of the hoardings and had also initiated steps to conduct an inspection and stability test through the Public Works Department. According to learned counsel for the petitioner, the petitioner has not violated any statutory provisions. While so, at the instigation of the third respondent, the official respondents are threatening the petitioner with demolition of hoarding, that too, without following due process of law.

5. It appears that before erection of advertisement board, the petitioner has not obtained any permission from the competent authorities and, in this regard, the first respondent Municipality had issued a notice on 22.8.2025 calling upon the petitioner to produce proof of permission obtained. In their reply dated 2.9.2025, the petitioner has stated that they undertake to apply for necessary approvals/permissions from Mangadu Municipality in due course. In their further letter dated 6.10.2025 addressed to the first respondent, the petitioner has stated that the current unipole hoarding erected by them falls within the exemption under the provisions of Section 117-Q of Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Act, 1998. The application of the petitioner was placed before the Single Window Approval Committee. On 9.12.2025, the first respondent addressed a letter to the Inspector of Police, T14, Mangadu Police Station to render necessary protection/security for removal of the hoarding on 18.12.2025.

6. The records reveal that the third respondent had filed complaint/appeal petition before the Ombudsman of the Tamil Nadu Panchayat Forum alleging illegal erection of advertisement boards/hoardings by the petitioner - Cybercity Housing Private Limited and one M/s. Sriram Properties, Mangadu. In the said proceedings, the representative of the petitioner appeared in person and placed on record certain documents. During enquiry, the Ombudsman had also recorded statement of the representative of the petitioner. After considering the documents and the statement placed before it, the Ombudsman observed as under:

“It is evident from the report of the Mangadu Municipal Commissioner that based on the submission of documents of the place where the advertising banners are erected, the place where the advertising banners are erected is known to be the place owned by the Cyber City Company, and that in the letter dated 06.10.2025 from Cyber City Company, an exemption has been granted under the above Act for placing a company's commercial advertisement under Section 117Q Exemption of the Tamil Nadu Urban Local Bodies Act.”

7. The order of the Ombudsman further states that although exemption has been granted for the erection of the above banners under Section 117 of the Act, it is the primary duty of the municipal officials concerned to examine whether the size and nature of the banners are as stipulated under the law and take action to ensure that the public is not inconvenienced by the said banners and that steps be taken to ensure the safety of the public. Considering the statement made on behalf of the petitioner, the Ombudsman directed the Municipal Commissioner of Mangadu to conduct a field survey to ascertain whether the banners are located within the limits specified in Section 117 of the Act. Thereafter, on 2.1.2026, the first respondent addressed a letter to the Executive Engineer, PWD, Kancheepuram to conduct an inspection of the hoardings and arch erected at the entrance of Mangadu Kunrathur Main Road, Mangadu “A” Village.

8. The submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner has not violated any of the provisions and that the first respondent is repeatedly issuing letters/notices to demolish the arch put up by the petitioner company, which is subject to test by the PWD authorities to find out its stability, and this continuous harassment by issuance of proceedings by the first respondent, at the instance of the third respondent, is causing grave hardship to the petitioner.

9. Issuance of the notices/letters by the first respondent to the petitioner and the inspection of the structure/arch/hoarding/advertisement board by the PWD authorities are measures initiated pursuant to the order passed by the Ombudsman. It is not in dispute that till date the petitioner has not chosen to assail the order of the Ombudsman dated 23.12.2025. Further, the authorities have power to examine the size and nature of the structure/arch/hoarding/advertisement board/unipoles to know whether the same is within the prescribed size and/or causing public inconvenience/safety measures.

10. Whether or not the petitioner had put up unauthorised hoarding/advertisement board/unipoles is to be decided by the authorities on physical examination of the area in question. If really, the petitioner is aggrieved by the order of the Ombudsman, it is for the petitioner to take recourse in accordance with law. As stated supra, in the present writ petition, the petitioner is seeking relief in respect of the entire 27.59 acres of land which was stated to be developed by the petitioner. If the respondent authorities initiate action against the entire extent of land alleging any violation, it is always open for the petitioner to challenge the same. Without any cause of action having arisen, seeking an omnibus direction from this court is premature.

For all the reasons stated above, there is no merit in the present writ petition and, therefore, the same is dismissed. No costs. Consequently, interim application is closed.
